Recognise the most frequent traps of the 7 official topics and of the prerequisites (SQL, Git, YAML, Jinja): 145 traps, each with the chapter that teaches it.
Use the last 7 days well, pass the exam-day checklist, and know what happens after the exam.
Imagine two candidates who know exactly the same things about dbt. The first one reads every question from top to bottom, answers

too quickly in DOMC questions, misses the word "only" in a selection question and spends six minutes on one long log. She finishes question 60 when the time is over. The second one reads the stem first, predicts the answer, keeps an eye on the clock and guesses smartly when she is not sure. The difference between them is easily six or eight questions: the difference between 62% (fail) and 74% (pass). Knowledge is necessary, but
turns knowledge into points. This chapter gives you that strategy, and then a list of 145 traps: the condensed error notebook of the whole bible.

Every exam question tests one sub-objective, and a few words in the question (such as "only", "first-degree", "default" or "without rebuilding") decide which option is right. Read the stem first, predict the answer, then judge each option on its own: in DOMC this is the only way, because you see one option at a time and cannot go back. Keep a steady pace (question 22 by minute 40 and question 44 by minute 80 at the latest), never leave a question empty, and spend your last week on the traps of this chapter instead of new topics.

c: Scenario questions are usually built with the same recipe. If you know the recipe, you know where to look. A typical scenario question has four parts:

blocks.alt: The four parts of a scenario question and the order to read them. On the page the parts are Scenario, Evidence, Stem, Options. Read them in this order: 1. the Stem (the real question, usually the last sentence, with the question mark): read it first, name the objective, circle the keywords; 2. the Scenario (the story: a team, a project, a problem to solve), with the question already in mind; 3. the Evidence (code, YAML, a log, a command or its output): look for the detail the stem asks about; 4. the Options (one correct answer, sometimes more, and several plausible wrong answers): predict first, then eliminate.

A scenario question is like a letter at the post office. The scenario is the envelope (who, where), the evidence is the parcel (what is inside), and the stem is the address (where it must go). A postman who reads the address first knows immediately what to look for in the parcel. A postman who opens every parcel first loses time.

DOMC (Discrete Option Multiple Choice) is the format that costs the most points to unprepared candidates. Remember the mechanics from
: one option at a time, a YES or NO for each, no way back, and the question may end early once your answers decide the result.

blocks.alt: How a DOMC question works: the stem is shown (read it twice) → one option appears → you answer YES or NO → if the result is decided, the question ends; if not, the next option appears. There is no way back to an answered option.

First pass. Answer every question. When a question needs more than about 3 minutes, choose your best option, mark it for review (if the interface offers it) and continue.

A question with 30 lines of logs is not necessarily hard: often the answer is in the first error line. But it can eat 6 minutes if you read every line. The exam. Follow the exam-day checklist.

Learning a new topic in the last two days usually costs more than it brings: it mixes with what you know and creates doubt. If a topic is still weak at D−2, move the exam date (free on Talview up to 24 hours before the appointment) rather than cramming.

The exam is delivered online, through Talview, with a remote proctor (a person who watches through your webcam). The rules below come from the dbt certification FAQ and Talview's test-taker guide; read the current versions of both before your exam, because details can change.
The booking is confirmed in Talview: date, time and
. Convert the time to your local time, and be careful if a change of summer/winter time happens between booking and exam day.
Your computer passes the Talview system check. Prefer a personal computer: the security settings of a work laptop can block the exam.

A supported web browser: the study guide links to the list of browsers supported by Caveon (the exam platform); the dbt FAQ names Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari, and Talview's guide lists recent versions of Chrome and Edge. A recent Chrome satisfies both.
Webcam and microphone work. Your face is clearly visible and well lit.
Stable internet: Talview asks for about 5 Mbps up and down. Use a cable if you can, and ask the people at home not to stream videos during the exam.
A valid government-issued photo ID, with the same name as your registration.
A quiet, private room with a desk and a chair (not a bed or a sofa), where nobody will come in.
Restart the computer. Close every other application (mail, chat, music, cloud sync) and turn off notifications.
: no notes, no book, no phone, no second device, no smartwatch. The exam is not open book.
Toilet, glass of water before you sit down, phone in another room or out of reach and silent.
Log in a few minutes early: the check-in (ID, room scan) takes time.
Show your ID to the camera. Be ready to scan the room and the desk with the webcam when asked.
Stay in front of the camera, do not leave your seat, do not talk to anyone, do not read the questions aloud: these behaviours can be flagged by the proctor.
Follow your pacing plan: Q22 by minute 40 and Q44 by minute 80 at the latest. DOMC: decide each option the first time.
No empty answer at the end.
A technical problem? Stay calm, use the Talview support chat and follow the proctor's instructions. The dbt certification team can be reached by email (the address is in the dbt certification FAQ).
You see it immediately at the end: pass or fail, and your percentage of scored questions answered correctly. You do not see which questions you missed.
Congratulations! dbt Labs sends you a
, which you can add to LinkedIn, your CV or a personal website, and a digital certificate. The certification is valid for
from the date it is awarded. To keep it, a shorter

exists (1 hour instead of 2), only for people who earned the credential with the full exam. Its eligibility rules can change, so read them on the dbt certification page when your 2 years come to an end. Keep your practice project alive: new versions of dbt bring new features, and you will use them at work.
It happens to many good analytics engineers, and it is not the end of anything. Right after the exam, write down the

that felt difficult (not the questions: exam content is confidential, so never copy or share questions). Compare with your mock-exam weak topics, re-read those chapters, redo their labs and quizzes, take a mock again, and book a retake when you are back above 80%. Each attempt is paid again, so take the time to prepare.
Read the stem first, name the objective, circle the keywords, predict, then eliminate.
A few words decide many answers: "only", "directly/first-degree", "by default", "the first run", "without rebuilding", "without creating objects", "best practice", "NOT".
Eliminate invalid syntax, the wrong resource, the wrong direction or depth, old syntax, and options with one false half.
DOMC: one option at a time, no way back. Make a full sentence with the stem; partially true or true-but-irrelevant is NO.
Pacing: first pass about 75 minutes, second pass about 30, final check about 10. Safety checkpoints: Q22 by minute 40, Q44 by minute 80.
Mark at most about 15 questions, always answer before you mark, and never leave a blank: there is no penalty for a wrong answer.
The 145 traps are the misconceptions that distractors are built from: go through them twice in the last week.
The last week is for light review; D−2 is the technical check (Talview, browser, webcam, internet, ID, room); D−1 is rest.
After a pass: Accredible badge, valid 2 years, then a shorter renewal exam. After a fail: note the weak topics, never the questions.
